about: Firmware (BIOS) settings Rig offers, by maker. One table for the server, the app (packages/core/src/firmware.ts) and the helper (helper/RigHelper/Firmware.cs). A step names a setting by its key here and a value by its key in `values`; the helper turns them into the maker's exact attribute name and value text for this PC's maker, and nothing else is ever sent to the firmware.

`allow`: the values a step may set. A value in `values` that isn't allowed has words in `refuse`, and is refused as never. `sealed`: BitLocker and device encryption measure it. No firmware change, and no restart into firmware setup, is made while drive encryption is on for the system drive or Rig can't tell. `undo: false`: Rig won't set the old value back (that would be a refused value), and says so. `windows`: what Windows itself can read after the restart to tell whether it took (tpm, secureBoot, virtualization); without it, Rig reads the maker's value again. `does`: Rig's own sentence for each value, shown on the card in place of Claude's, for a setting Rig offers itself (the battery charge limit, from a laptop's Battery life tab).

Per maker: `attribute` is the exact name the maker's class uses and `values` the exact value text for each Rig value. `fromWindows: false` means the maker doesn't let Windows change it without a firmware password, which Rig never uses: it is read only, and `why` says so. `asks`: the firmware asks the person to confirm at the next start. `stopsAt`: the charge level the maker's value stops at, when the maker documents one.

`makers`: how a PC's maker is found (`match`, folded, against Win32_ComputerSystem.Manufacturer's start). `never`: words that are never a setting Rig changes, matched against a step's setting and against every attribute name here (folded, letters and digits only).

virtualization.name: Virtualization (Intel VT-x or AMD-V)
virtualization.says: Lets the processor run virtual machines, WSL 2, Windows Sandbox and Android apps.

vtd.name: Direct device access for virtual machines (VT-d)
vtd.says: Lets virtual machines use a device directly. Some security features use it too.

wakeOnLan.name: Wake on LAN
wakeOnLan.says: Lets another device on your network turn this PC on.

fanMode.name: Fan and cooling mode
fanMode.says: How the firmware trades fan noise for cooling.

chargeLimit.name: Battery charge limit
chargeLimit.says: A battery kept at 100% on the charger wears fastest; most makers let it stop at about 80%.

does.on: Stops charging short of full while it's plugged in, so the battery wears more slowly.
does.off: Charges the battery to full again.

values.off: Let HP manage my battery charging

tpm.name: Security chip (TPM)
tpm.says: Windows 11, BitLocker and Windows Hello need it.

refuse.off: Rig never turns the security chip (TPM) off: Windows 11, BitLocker and Windows Hello depend on it

dell.why: Dell lets Windows change the security chip only with a BIOS admin password, which Rig never uses. Turn it on in firmware setup.

hp.asks: HP asks you to press a key at the next start to confirm.

lenovo.why: Lenovo lets Windows change security settings only with a supervisor password, which Rig never uses. Turn it on in firmware setup.

secureBoot.name: Secure Boot
secureBoot.says: Lets only signed start-up code run. Windows 11 and some games' anti-cheat need it.

refuse.off: Rig never turns Secure Boot off, which lowers this PC's protection and can stop some games running

hp.asks: HP asks you to press a key at the next start to confirm.

lenovo.why: Lenovo lets Windows change security settings only with a supervisor password, which Rig never uses. Turn it on in firmware setup.

never.says: Rig never clears the security chip (TPM) or switches it between the processor and a separate chip, which loses the keys BitLocker and Windows Hello keep in it
Rig never changes Secure Boot's mode or keys, which can stop Windows starting
Rig never switches between UEFI and legacy start-up (CSM), which can stop Windows starting
Rig never changes the storage controller's mode (SATA, RAID, AHCI, VMD), which can stop Windows finding its drive
Rig never changes the boot order or boot entries, which can stop Windows starting
Rig never sets, changes or clears firmware passwords
Rig never changes Absolute (Computrace) or anti-theft settings, which often can't be undone
Rig never changes memory profiles, voltages or clock speeds in firmware, which can stop this PC starting or damage it
Rig never updates or rewrites the firmware itself
